newsitem.title: CHINA: China to hunt suspect books ahead of party congres.
newsitem.headline: China to hunt suspect books ahead of party congres.

text.p: China is preparing a crackdown on politically suspect, pornographic and pirated publications ahead of a crucial Communist Party congress in September or October, the People's Daily said on Wednesday.

Beijing city authorities were determined to clamp down in order to "welcome the victorious opening of the 15th Party Congress with a healthy and orderly publishing market", the official newspaper said.
"From the middle of August to the beginning of October a focused investigation of the publishing market will be opened across the whole city," it said.
"Books, periodicals, audio-visual products and electronic articles that have serious political problems will be uncovered and dealt with strictly," it said.

Chinese publications officials have struggled to stem a flood of pirated, pornographic and banned products flowing into Beijing, where top leaders are set to meet to chart the nation's political course at the five-yearly party congress.

Controls on activities judged illegal or socially harmful are usually stepped up in the capital ahead of international or major domestic events and are likely to be especially tight during the congress, expected in late September or early October.
Authorities in the capital had already netted 1,386 people accused of creating or dealing in suspect publishing products since the latter part of 1996, the People's Daily said.
Officials had seized 269,622 banned books and periodicals and 509,611 illegal audio-visual or electronic products, it said.
Despite repeated calls for tougher controls on banned books, book buyers say many volumes dealing with sensitive political issues or explicit sexuality remained widely available.
Streetside compact disc and computer software salesmen continue to hawk illicit goods in defiance of a nationwide crackdown on piracy partly prompted by pressure from the United States.
